data.title: Huntington Ingalls wins $336M contract for long-lead carrier materials
data.description:
• Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII) announced on Friday that it won a $336.11M undefinitized contract for long-lead materials to support construction of the future USS William J. Clinton (CVN 82).
  • The contract covers advance procurement of materials needed for the aircraft carrier’s construction in Newport News, Virginia.
  • The work is expected to be completed by March 2039, with the full $336.11M in fiscal 2026 Navy shipbuilding funds obligated at award.
  • Naval Sea Systems Command is the contracting activity.

data.title: Northrop Grumman lands 9-year, $508.49M missile defense deal
data.description:
• Northrop Grumman's (NOC) unit secured a $508.49M follow-on contract from the Missile Defense Agency.
  • The contract covers flight test support for remaining ballistic missile targets and logistics support for government-furnished equipment used in missile defense testing.
  • The contract runs from September 2026 through August 2035 and includes cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost-reimbursable, and fixed-price incentive components.
  • A total of $8.79M in fiscal 2026 research, development, test, and evaluation funds is being obligated on the award.
  • The Missile Defense Agency is the contracting activity.

data.title: Matinas BioPharma gets 2027 window to restore NYSE American listing compliance
data.description:
• Matinas BioPharma Holdings (MTNB) announced on Friday that it received a non-compliant notice from NYSE American for falling below its stockholders’ equity requirement.
  • The company had $1.8M in stockholders’ equity as of June 30, below the required $2.0M, and has reported losses in each of its past five fiscal years.
  • NYSE American has given the company until October 2, 2027, to regain compliance under its existing plan.
  • The notice has no immediate impact on the stock’s listing or the company’s operations. However, failure to regain compliance could lead to delisting proceedings.

data.title: Ionis Pharmaceuticals falls after Pelacarsen fails key Phase 3 heart trial
data.description:
• Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS) announced on Friday that partner Novartis' pelacarsen failed to meet the main goal of its Phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial, as it did not reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events versus placebo.
  • The drug successfully lowered Lp(a) levels, but this did not lead to a reduction in heart-related events compared with the placebo.
  • The result is a major setback for pelacarsen, which was being developed for people with high Lp(a), an inherited risk factor linked to heart disease that affects about 20% of people worldwide.
  • Pelacarsen showed an acceptable safety profile, with full trial results expected to be presented at a future medical meeting.
  • Shares of Ionis Pharmaceuticals fell 6.18% to about $54.50 in after-hours trading following the announcement.

data.title: Airbus reaches preliminary deal with Spanish unions
data.description:
Airbus (EADSF) (EADSY) reached a preliminary deal with four unions in Spain, Reuters reported Friday, marking a potential breakthrough in a dispute that has triggered weeks of strikes at the company's Spanish plants.

The company said it reached a "proposal of understanding" ​with unions UGT, ATP, CCOO, and SIPA after a meeting mediated by the Industry Ministry to resolve a labor dispute over ​pay and conditions following months of negotiations.

The proposal will be submitted to the ​entire workforce for a binding referendum, Airbus (EADSF) (EADSY) reportedly said ​in a memo sent to its ⁠staff in Spain.

Separately, Reuters also reported that Airbus (EADSF) (EADSY) has been forced to slow deliveries of its A330neo jet after a stray tool was discovered in the tail section of an aircraft in production during a pre-delivery inspection.

"We confirm we recently identified an isolated quality ​issue on an A330 horizontal tail plane," the company said in ⁠a statement. "This led us to inspect A330s in the production process, slowing ​down monthly deliveries over the summer. The root cause is identified and A330 deliveries ​have resumed."

The horizontal tail plane is made in Airbus's (EADSF) (EADSY) Spanish facilities, although the discovery ​likely is not related ⁠to the recent strikes at the company's Spanish plants.

data.title: Fair Isaac slumps 17% on VantageScore directive
data.description:
Fair Isaac (FICO), a global analytics and decisioning-software company, retreated almost 17% on Friday, after Federal Housing Director Bill Pulte directed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to allow all lenders to use the competing VantageScore credit-scoring system. The directive landed as a direct challenge to FICO's pricing power in mortgage originations, one of its most concentrated revenue streams.

The stock closed at $932.26, a decline of $186.67 on the session.
